page: Microsoft Azure D2alds_v7 is an x86_64 architecture server instance belonging to the Daldsv7 family. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor running at 4.5 GHz, featuring 2 vCPUs mapped to 1 physical core with 2 threads per core under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is configured with a dedicated CPU allocation, 4.0 GB of system memory yielding 2.0 GB per core, and 118 GB of local storage. It is also Premium Storage capable.

Benchmark data reveals a significant contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. The high clock speed of the AMD EPYC processor enables top-tier single-core performance, as demonstrated by stress-ng single-core CPU tests, gzip compression, and bzip3 decompression, all ranking in the top 10%. Conversely, multi-core CPU performance, PassMark CPU scores, and PassMark memory scores fall into the bottom 25% due to the low core count. Memory bandwidth is average for large blocks but weak for small cached blocks.

With a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, this instance represents a low-memory, compute-focused configuration. It offers qualitative cost efficiency for workloads that require high single-threaded performance but do not demand large memory footprints or massive parallelization. Tradeoffs include weak performance in database operations, static web serving, and multi-core tasks. This server is best suited for lightweight single-threaded processing, basic utility scripting, or small-scale applications requiring fast single-core execution and moderate local storage.
